clue.text: Adventurous thing for house-breaker to do, using jemmy

parts.note: a burglar's job is to get in, that is to enter the house
a jemmy is a crowbar, used for prising doors and windows open

explanation.surface: Breaking and entering with a crowbar is described as a bold venture.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a description of burglary; only 'Adventurous' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone bold and full of initiative, ready to take on new ventures.

clue.text: Passes point and slips

parts.note: E (east) is one of the compass points
slips or small mistakes are lapses

explanation.surface: Someone passes a point on a track and slips over.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that goes by is said to pass or slip away; both are verbs of time running on.

clue.text: Army contractor ?

parts.note: read 'Army' as 'of the arm': a muscle in the upper arm that contracts to straighten the elbow

explanation.surface: A firm supplying goods to the military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Army' looks like the military, but it means belonging to the arm; the contractor is a muscle, which contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle at the back of the upper arm works by contracting.

clue.text: Meat and drink, kept as ordered

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new order, so the letters of kept as are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food and drink are served just as the customer asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a waiter taking an order; it is the anagram signal, and 'and' and the first 'as' are joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef from the hindquarters is a kind of meat.

clue.text: About to get a title ? Bit of a step up !

indicators.note: in a down clue, up tells the solver to read the pieces from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: Someone about to be knighted is going up in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the pieces round because this is a down entry. 'Bit of a step up' suggests promotion, but the definition is the vertical part of a stair.
explanation.definitionFit: On a staircase the vertical board between two treads is called the riser, one part of each step.

clue.text: Island is rough for cars too

indicators.note: rough means roughly handled, so the letters of cars too are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: An island's roads are so rough they are hard on cars too.
explanation.walkthrough: SOCOTRA is an island in the Arabian Sea off the Horn of Africa; 'is' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sizeable island in the Arabian Sea, belonging to Yemen.

clue.text: "The —— Roman of them all" (J Caesar)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Mark Antony's tribute over the body of Brutus at the end of Shakespeare's Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: A line quoted from Shakespeare's Julius Caesar with one word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a quotation to complete, not wordplay: Antony praises Brutus as the most honourable of the conspirators.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony calls Brutus the most honourable and high-minded Roman, the finest in character of them all.

clue.text: Novel Sussex coastal feature ?

definitions.meaning: a 1938 novel by Graham Greene set in the seaside town
a stick of hard pink sweet sold at the seaside resort on the Sussex coast, its name lettered through it

explanation.surface: A new landmark has appeared on the Sussex coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, and 'coastal feature' suggests a cliff; both are traps. Brighton is a resort on the south coast of England, and seaside rock is a hard stick of candy.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene's book and the striped candy sold on Brighton's seafront share the same name.

clue.text: Possibly Mr Lea is taking the practical view

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of Mr Lea is may form something else when reordered

explanation.surface: A certain Mr Lea is being sensible and down to earth about things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges all seven letters of MR LEA IS; 'taking' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is the attitude of facing facts as they are, a pragmatic outlook.

clue.text: Old musical instrument — or container only ?

parts.note: a sack is a bag, a container
but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether an antique object is a musical instrument or just a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' joins the definition to the wordplay. A sackbut is the early form of the trombone.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is a Renaissance brass instrument, the forerunner of the trombone.

clue.text: Somebody content with a chair and a book?

definitions.meaning: an academic who is satisfied to hold a university chair, the top teaching post
an early novel by Charlotte Brontë, published after her death

explanation.surface: Someone happy just to sit in a chair with a good book.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a reader in an armchair; the chair is a professorship, and the book is Charlotte Brontë's first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A university chair is held by a senior academic, and Brontë's novel bears that title with the article.

clue.text: Effusive people of oily type ?

definitions.meaning: people who pour out emotion or praise in a rush
oil wells from which crude oil spouts freely

explanation.surface: Smarmy, slippery people who are too effusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oily type' suggests an unctuous person, but it is an oil well that spouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To gush is to pour out, whether words of enthusiasm or a jet of crude oil from a well.

clue.text: Little Russian hunter out : East

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of hunter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small Russian hunter is out in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HUNTER into RUTHEN, then E is added. 'Little Russian' is an old name for a Ukrainian or Ruthenian, not a short person.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthenians, once called Little Russians, were East Slavs of the Ukraine and Carpathian region.

clue.text: They are found growing round the trunk

definitions.text: They are found growing round the trunk

parts.words: They are found growing round the trunk
parts.note: read 'trunk' as an elephant's nose, not a tree: the long ivory teeth that grow either side of it

explanation.surface: Something growing round a tree trunk, like ivy or fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' pulls the mind to trees; it is an elephant's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: An elephant's long ivory teeth grow out from the jaw on either side of its trunk.

clue.text: Sorcerer finds René backward about song

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around the other
backward tells the solver to write the name from its last letter to its first

parts.note: the French name René is taken for its letters
a chant is a song, often a repetitive one

explanation.surface: A magician finds a Frenchman called René lagging behind over a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' reverses the name and 'about' wraps the result round the song. 'finds' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: One who casts spells, a wizard or magician, is an enchanter.

clue.text: Satisfied to carry in some of the earth

indicators.note: to carry means to hold something inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: content means satisfied
in is taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener happy to carry soil indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: CONTENT holds IN, making CONT-IN-ENT. 'some of the earth' is a definition by part: one landmass among several.
explanation.definitionFit: The land surface of the world is divided into a handful of great landmasses such as Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Little lad joins relatives in a dram

parts.note: a nipper is a small boy
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A small boy joins his family in having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' and 'in' are joining words. A nipperkin is an old word for a small measure of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A nipperkin was a small measure of wine or spirits, about a half-pint or less, much like a tot.

clue.text: Second-rate tennis dance in Dublin ?

parts.note: Pat is the stock crossword name for an Irishman, so a dance in Dublin is Pat's ball
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A poor game of tennis is likened to a dance in Ireland's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat, short for Patrick, is the traditional nickname for an Irishman, so a Dublin dance is a Pat ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Patball is slow, gentle tennis with the ball patted back and forth, poor standard play.

clue.text: Play parts in Lear, etc

indicators.note: parts means breaks up, so the letters of Lear, etc are split and recombined

explanation.surface: Acting roles in King Lear and other dramas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' seems to be a verb with 'parts' as its object, but it is the definition; 'parts' breaks up LEAR ETC, and 'in' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a tragedy by Sophocles, and another by Euripides, both ancient Greek stage works.

clue.text: Banter in which affection appears

indicators.note: in tells the solver the answer sits inside the run of letters across the words which affection

explanation.surface: Friendly teasing that shows how much people care for each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a description of affectionate ribbing, but the answer runs across the join of 'which' and 'affection'; 'appears' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaff someone is to tease them good-naturedly, the joshing of friends.

clue.text: Humming-bird with, an unusual rib coil

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of rib coil should be arranged in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A humming-bird with an odd coiled rib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with an' are joining words; 'unusual' rearranges RIB COIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Colibri is the French-derived name for a humming-bird, used for several tropical species.

clue.text: Makes certain fool rues error

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: error means the letters of rues are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A fool regrets a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' scrambles the second word, which follows the fool; the surface reads as one sentence about regret.
explanation.definitionFit: To assure is to make sure or guarantee, removing doubt.

clue.text: At the inn their charges were for coaching, perhaps

definitions.text: At the inn their charges were for coaching, perhaps

parts.words: At the inn their charges were for coaching, perhaps
parts.note: read 'charges' as the animals in someone's care and 'coaching' as pulling stagecoaches: the stablemen of old coaching inns

explanation.surface: An innkeeper's bill includes fees for training lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' looks like prices on a bill and 'coaching' like tuition; they are the horses in the stablemen's care, used to draw coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Stablemen at a coaching inn looked after travellers' horses, which drew the stagecoaches.

clue.text: It's a boy ! Next one, a girl

parts.note: the announcement of a birth of a son
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Parents announce a baby boy and hope the next one will be a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Next' is a joining word placing I after SON; the definition is the girl's name Sonia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonia is a female first name, a girl's name of Russian origin.

clue.text: Complaints made about poor Sue — treats people badly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: ills are complaints, ailments

indicators.note: poor means in bad shape, so the letters of Sue are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grievances are raised about poor Sue, who mistreats people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns SUE into USE, and ILLS goes 'about' it; 'made' is a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-use is to mistreat or abuse, the verb matching 'treats badly'.

clue.text: Buster embraces redhead — Cherry

indicators.note: embraces means holds in its arms, so one name goes round a letter

parts.note: Buster Keaton was the deadpan star of silent film comedy
the head, or first letter, of red is R

explanation.surface: A silent film star hugs a red-haired woman named Cherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cherry' looks like a fruit or a woman's name; it is Cherry Kearton, the pioneer British wildlife photographer and filmmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry Kearton was an early wildlife photographer, and the surname is his.

clue.text: Prohibition therefore includes BMA members

indicators.note: includes means takes inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

indicators.note: members here means the separate letters of BMA, taken apart and put in a new order

explanation.surface: A ban is therefore imposed on doctors of the British Medical Association.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' shuffles the three initials, which go inside the Latin word after its first letter. The BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' professional body.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade with a country.

clue.text: Excuses article, attempts making jokes

parts.note: pleas are excuses offered in defence
an is the indefinite article
tries are attempts

explanation.surface: Someone makes excuses and attempts at humour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a joining word between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasantries are light witty remarks or polite jests made in conversation.
